summary: St-François Airport (SFC) is a small airfield serving the eastern tip of Grande-Terre in Guadeloupe, near the popular tourist commune of St-François. It primarily handles general aviation traffic, private flights, and small charter operations rather than scheduled commercial service. The airport sits close to the Atlantic coast, offering convenient access to nearby attractions including the La Pointe des Châteaux headland, championship golf courses, and the resort areas of eastern Grande-Terre.
faqs:
Q: Does St-François Airport have scheduled commercial flights?
A: No, St-François Airport is a small airfield primarily serving private, general aviation, and charter flights. Most visitors flying to Guadeloupe arrive through Pointe-à-Pitre International Airport (PTP).

Q: How far is St-François Airport from the town center?
A: The airport is located very close to St-François, typically just a few minutes' drive from the town center, marina, and main beach areas.

Q: Are car rentals available at St-François Airport?
A: As a small general aviation facility, rental car services may be limited on-site, so it's advisable to arrange a vehicle in advance or arrange ground transport with your accommodation.

Q: What is the airport used for today?
A: The airport supports private aviation, flight training, and occasional charter flights, serving the local tourism and leisure market in eastern Guadeloupe.
transport_tips: Renting a car is the most practical way to reach and explore the area, as St-François is spread out and public transport options in eastern Grande-Terre are limited. Taxis can be arranged in advance or requested upon arrival, though availability may be limited compared to larger airports. If flying in privately, coordinate ground transport with your hotel or charter operator ahead of time.
local_tip: Time your visit to catch sunset at nearby La Pointe des Châteaux, just a short drive east of the airport—it's one of the most dramatic coastal viewpoints in the Caribbean, with the Atlantic crashing against limestone formations.
